purpose: Test whether the rotational-block proxy responds to bearing geometry in an independently solved PnP problem, while exposing point-count, image-noise, outlier, and camera-intrinsic boundaries.

bearing_layouts.wide_bearing: normalized x uniform [-0.50,0.50], normalized y uniform [-0.35,0.35]
bearing_layouts.horizontal_line: normalized x uniform [-0.50,0.50], normalized y Gaussian sigma 0.005
bearing_layouts.vertical_line: normalized x Gaussian sigma 0.005, normalized y uniform [-0.35,0.35]

solver.outlier_policy: For the outlier sweep, replace the declared fraction of image observations with uniform image coordinates; do not change the proxy input geometry.
solver.valid_trial: solvePnP returns true and finite rotation/translation vectors

proxy.formula: lambda_min(H_rr)/lambda_max(H_rr) from the same pinhole rotational Jacobian block as the runtime implementation

outputs: condition median, RMSE, 2.5th percentile, and 97.5th percentile
Spearman rho without frame-level or trial-level significance claims

predeclared_checks.geometry_response: median proxy for wide_bearing must exceed clustered_bearing
predeclared_checks.independent_rotation_response: median rotation error for wide_bearing must be lower than clustered_bearing at nominal settings
predeclared_checks.boundary_point_count: report whether error changes with count while the normalized spectral proxy remains similar
predeclared_checks.boundary_noise: report error growth although the geometry-only proxy is unchanged for paired geometry
predeclared_checks.boundary_outliers: report error growth although the geometry-only proxy does not encode corrupted match measurements
predeclared_checks.boundary_intrinsics: report uniform focal-scale invariance of the ratio and any anisotropic-intrinsic dependence

decision.pass: The proxy may remain a descriptive directional-geometry axis with the recorded boundaries; it is not confidence, covariance, or formal observability.
decision.fail: Remove the third axis from the core incremental-value claim and reassess whether a two-axis protocol is sufficient.
